title: Low-Overhead General-Purpose Near-Data Processing in CXL Memory Expanders
problem: CXL memory expansion suffers from latency overhead for memory-bound applications. Existing NDP solutions are either application-specific or inefficient (using full CPU/GPU cores), and PCIe/CXL.io communication incurs microsecond-scale latency unsuitable for fine-grained offloading.
motivation: CXL enables cost-efficient memory expansion, but performance limitations for memory-bound workloads require practical low-latency near-data processing.
method: The solution embeds processing capability directly into CXL memory controllers (the devices managing external memory expansion), enabling general-purpose computation without needing application-specific designs or wasting full CPU/GPU cores. Rather than using the slow PCIe/CXL.io communication links that add microseconds of delay, it introduces a faster direct connection between the host and the memory controller. This allows the system to offload small, fine-grained pieces of computation to the memory controller with minimal latency, processing data where it's stored rather than moving it back to the main processor.
key_novelty: Embedding general-purpose processing directly in CXL memory controllers with a low-latency communication link that replaces slower PCIe/CXL.io paths, making it practical to offload fine-grained computations to the memory source.
contributions: First general-purpose NDP architecture for CXL memory suitable for diverse applications
Novel low-latency communication mechanism for fine-grained host-CXL NDP offloading
Cost-effective design optimized for memory-bound workloads without full CPU/GPU cores
Evaluation on latency-sensitive and bandwidth-intensive applications
limitations: Performance metrics and specific baseline comparisons not discussed in abstract
primary_theme: low-latency general-purpose near-data processing in CXL memory
